{{short description|Danish mathematician}}
{{for|the Norwegian journalist|Carsten Thomassen (journalist)}}
'''Carsten Thomassen''' (born August 22, 1948 in [[Grindsted]]) is a [[Denmark|Danish]] [[mathematician]]. He has been a  Professor of Mathematics at the [[Technical University of Denmark]] since 1981, and since 1990 a member of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]]. His research concerns [[discrete mathematics]] and more specifically graph theory.<ref>[http://www2.mat.dtu.dk/people/C.Thomassen/ Carsten Thomassen's home page]</ref>

Thomassen received his [[Ph.D.]] in 1976 from the [[University of Waterloo]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=43907}}</ref>

He is editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of Graph Theory]]'' and the ''[[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]]'', and editor of ''[[Combinatorica]]'', the ''[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]'' Series B, [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]], and the ''[[European Journal of Combinatorics]]''.

He was awarded the Dedicatory Award of the 6th International Conference on the Theory and Applications of Graphs by the [[Western Michigan University]] in May 1988, the [[Lester R. Ford Award]] by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 1993,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Thomassen, Carsten|title=The Jordan-Schoenflies Theorem and the classification of surfaces|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=99|year=1992|issue=2 |pages=116–130|doi=10.2307/2324180|jstor=2324180 |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/the-jordan-sch-nflies-theorem-and-the-classification-of-surfaces|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and the Faculty of Mathematics Alumni Achievement Medal by the University of Waterloo in 2005. In 1990, he was an invited speaker (''Graphs, random walks and electric networks'') at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in [[Kyōto]]. He was included on the [[ISI Web of Knowledge]] list  of the 250 most cited mathematicians.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highlycited.com/categories/mathematics/|title=Mathematics category list|work=[[ISIHighlyCited.com]]|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111204141252/http://highlycited.com/categories/mathematics/|archivedate=2011-12-04}}</ref>

==Selected works==
*with Bojan Mohar: ''Graphs on Surfaces'', Johns Hopkins University Press, 2001
*5-choosability of planar graphs (see [[List coloring]])
*works on [[Hypohamiltonian graph]]s
*Hamilton connectivity of Tournaments (see [[Tournament (graph theory)]]) and of 4-connected planar graphs
*his proof of [[Gr%C3%B6tzsch%27s theorem]]
